358	def run_migrations(dry_run: bool = False, schema_only: bool = False,
359	                   applied_by_session: str = None):
360	    if not DB_PATH.exists():
361	        print(f"ERROR: Database not found at {DB_PATH}", file=sys.stderr)
362	        sys.exit(1)
363	
364	    # isolation_level=None -- true autocommit. Without it, PRAGMA foreign_keys
365	    # is issued inside an implicit transaction and silently does nothing.
366	    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(DB_PATH), isolation_level=None)
367	    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
368	    current = get_user_version(conn)
369	    print(f"Current schema version: {current}")
370	
371	    # Walk the same plan the rebuild walks, so a DB that is behind catches up in
372	    # the same order CI reproduces. Applying pending-schema-then-pending-data
373	    # here while the rebuild honours AFTER_DATA would let the two paths disagree
374	    # — which is precisely the divergence the reproducibility gate exists to
375	    # catch, and it would surface as a mystery rather than as this bug.
376	    plan = build_plan()
377	    have_dm = data_migrations_table_exists(conn)
378	    applied = applied_data_migrations(conn) if have_dm else set()
379	    final_schema, applied_count, skipped_data = current, 0, 0
380	
381	    print("\n--- Migrations ---")
382	    for step in plan:
383	        if step[0] == "schema":
384	            _, version, path = step
385	            if version <= current:
386	                continue
387	            print(f"    Applying {path.name} (→ version {version})...")
388	            if not dry_run:
389	                stmts, declared_uv = _prepare_body(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
390	                # Baselines declare their own user_version inside the script;
391	                # honour it. Non-baseline migrations follow the filename number.
392	                stamp = declared_uv if "baseline" in path.name else version
393	                # Advisory only on the schema path: adding a blocking referential
394	                # gate here is OD-7/D7, a separate owner decision, not this fix.
395	                _apply_atomically(conn, stmts, label=path.name,
396	                                  user_version=stamp, fk_blocking=False)
397	            final_schema = version
398	            continue
399	
400	        _, _ts, migration_id, path = step
401	        if schema_only:
402	            # Everything after a data step may be gated behind it (AFTER_DATA),
403	            # so --schema-only stops here rather than applying a later schema
404	            # migration out of order and leaving user_version claiming a schema
405	            # the DB does not have. With no AFTER_DATA marker every data step is
406	            # already at the tail, so this is the old behaviour exactly.
407	            skipped_data = sum(1 for s in plan[plan.index(step):] if s[0] == "data")
408	            gated_schema = sum(1 for s in plan[plan.index(step):] if s[0] == "schema")
409	            if gated_schema:
410	                print(f"  [--schema-only stops here: {gated_schema} schema migration(s) are "
411	                      f"gated behind data migrations by AFTER_DATA. Run without --schema-only.]")
412	            break
413	        if not have_dm:
414	            have_dm = data_migrations_table_exists(conn)
415	            if not have_dm:
416	                print("  [skip data migration — data_migrations table not present yet]")
417	                continue
418	            applied = applied_data_migrations(conn)
419	        if migration_id in applied:
420	            continue
421	        print(f"    Applying {path.name}...")
422	        if not dry_run:
423	            _apply_one_data_migration(conn, migration_id, path, applied_by_session)
424	        applied_count += 1
425	
426	    if schema_only:
427	        print(f"\n--- {skipped_data} data migration(s) skipped (--schema-only) ---")
428	
429	    conn.close()
430	    suffix = " [DRY-RUN]" if dry_run else ""
431	    print(f"\nDone.{suffix} Schema at version {final_schema}; {applied_count} data migration(s) applied.")
432

434	def rebuild_from_migrations(target_db_path: str, dry_run: bool = False):
435	    """Build a DB from scratch by applying every migration in order. Used by CI."""
436	    target = Path(target_db_path)
437	    if target.exists() and not dry_run:
438	        target.unlink()
439	    print(f"Rebuilding {target} from migration history...")
440	    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(target), isolation_level=None)
441	    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
442	
443	    # Replay in the faithful order, which is schema-then-data except where a
444	    # migration declares AFTER_DATA (see build_plan).
445	    plan = build_plan()
446	    n_schema = sum(1 for s in plan if s[0] == "schema")
447	    n_data = len(plan) - n_schema
448	    print(f"  Applying {n_schema} schema migration(s) and {n_data} data migration(s)")
449	    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec='seconds')
450	    for step in plan:
451	        if step[0] == "schema":
452	            _, version, path = step
453	            if not dry_run:
454	                stmts, declared_uv = _prepare_body(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
455	                stamp = declared_uv if "baseline" in path.name else version
456	                _apply_atomically(conn, stmts, label=path.name,
457	                                  user_version=stamp, fk_blocking=False)
458	            continue
459	
460	        _, ts, migration_id, path = step
461	        if not data_migrations_table_exists(conn):
462	            continue  # pre-007: nothing to record against
463	        body = path.read_bytes()
464	        sha = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()
465	        text = body.decode('utf-8')
466	        if not dry_run:
467	            statements, _uv = _prepare_body(text)
468	            is_bootstrap = "BOOTSTRAP" in text[:500].upper()
469	            ledger = (
470	                "INSERT INTO data_migrations (migration_id, applied_at, content_sha,"
471	                " applied_by_session, notes) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
472	                (migration_id, now, sha, None, "rebuilt by runner"),
473	            )
474	            try:
475	                _apply_atomically(conn, statements, label=migration_id, ledger=ledger,
476	                                  fk_blocking=True, is_bootstrap=is_bootstrap)
477	            except sqlite3.Error as e:
478	                print(f"  ERROR applying {migration_id}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
479	                sys.exit(1)
480	
481	    conn.close()
482	    print(f"Rebuilt {target} successfully.")

485	def selftest() -> int:
486	    """Prove the transaction properties F5/F6 assert, rather than asserting them.
487	
488	    Each case states the defect it pins. Run: python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --selftest
489	    """
490	    import tempfile
491	    results, failures = [], 0
492	
493	    def check(name, cond, detail=""):
494	        nonlocal failures
495	        results.append((name, bool(cond), detail))
496	        if not cond:
497	            failures += 1
498	
499	    seq = [0]
500	
501	    def fresh(tmp):
502	        seq[0] += 1
503	        db = Path(tmp) / f"t{seq[0]}.db"
504	        c = sqlite3.connect(str(db), isolation_level=None)
505	        c.execute("CREATE TABLE parent (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY)")
506	        c.execute("CREATE TABLE child (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, "
507	                  "pid TEXT REFERENCES parent(id))")
508	        c.execute("CREATE TABLE data_migrations (migration_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, "
509	                  "applied_at TEXT, content_sha TEXT, applied_by_session TEXT, notes TEXT)")
510	        c.execute("INSERT INTO parent VALUES ('P1')")
511	        return c
512	
513	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
514	        # --- F5: a body that violates FK must leave NOTHING behind -------------
515	        c = fresh(tmp)
516	        body = ("-- Generated: test\n"
517	                "BEGIN TRANSACTION;\n"
518	                "INSERT INTO child VALUES ('C1','P1');\n"
519	                "INSERT INTO child VALUES ('C2','GHOST');\n"
520	                "COMMIT;\n")
521	        stmts, _ = _prepare_body(body)
522	        ledger = ("INSERT INTO data_migrations (migration_id, applied_at, content_sha,"
523	                  " applied_by_session) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", ("m1", "now", "sha", None))
524	        raised = False
525	        try:
526	            _apply_atomically(c, stmts, label="m1", ledger=ledger, fk_blocking=True)
527	        except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
528	            raised = True
529	        rows = c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM child").fetchone()[0]
530	        led = c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM data_migrations").fetchone()[0]
531	        check("F5 FK violation raises", raised)
532	        check("F5 body rolled back (the defect: this used to be 2)", rows == 0,
533	              f"child rows = {rows}")
534	        check("F5 ledger row rolled back", led == 0, f"ledger rows = {led}")
535	        check("F5 foreign_keys restored", c.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys").fetchone()[0] == 1)
536	        c.close()
537	
538	        # --- F5: a clean body commits body AND ledger together -----------------
539	        c = fresh(tmp)
540	        stmts, _ = _prepare_body("BEGIN TRANSACTION;\n"
541	                                 "INSERT INTO child VALUES ('C1','P1');\nCOMMIT;\n")
542	        _apply_atomically(c, stmts, label="m2", ledger=ledger, fk_blocking=True)
543	        check("F5 clean body commits", c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM child").fetchone()[0] == 1)
544	        check("F5 clean ledger commits",
545	              c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM data_migrations").fetchone()[0] == 1)
546	        c.close()
547	
548	        # --- F6: the file's own BEGIN/COMMIT is stripped, not nested -----------
549	        stmts, _ = _prepare_body("-- header comment\nBEGIN TRANSACTION;\n"
550	                                 "INSERT INTO child VALUES ('C9','P1');\nCOMMIT;\n")
551	        check("F6 wrapper stripped past the comment header",
552	              not any(_TXN_CTL.match(_code_of(s)) for s in stmts),
553	              f"statements = {stmts}")
554	
555	        # --- F6: PRAGMA foreign_keys is hoisted out of the body ----------------
556	        c = fresh(tmp)
557	        stmts, _ = _prepare_body("PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF;\n"
558	                                 "INSERT INTO child VALUES ('C1','P2');\n"
559	                                 "INSERT INTO parent VALUES ('P2');\n"
560	                                 "PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;\n")
561	        check("F6 fk pragmas hoisted out of body",
562	              not any(_PRAGMA_FK.match(_code_of(s)) for s in stmts))
563	        _apply_atomically(c, stmts, label="m3", fk_blocking=True)
564	        check("F6 out-of-order bulk load succeeds (pragma honoured in autocommit)",
565	              c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM child").fetchone()[0] == 1)
566	        c.close()
567	
568	        # --- F6: user_version stamp is atomic with the DDL ---------------------
569	        c = fresh(tmp)
570	        stmts, uv = _prepare_body("PRAGMA user_version = 42;\n"
571	                                  "CREATE TABLE ok (x);\n"
572	                                  "INSERT INTO child VALUES ('C3','GHOST');\n")
573	        check("F6 declared user_version captured", uv == 42, f"uv = {uv}")
574	        try:
575	            _apply_atomically(c, stmts, label="m4", user_version=uv, fk_blocking=True)
576	        except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
577	            pass
578	        check("F6 user_version rolled back with the DDL",
579	              c.execute("PRAGMA user_version").fetchone()[0] == 0,
580	              f"user_version = {c.execute('PRAGMA user_version').fetchone()[0]}")
581	        check("F6 DDL rolled back too",
582	              c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='ok'").fetchone()[0] == 0)
583	        c.close()
584	
585	        # --- splitter: a semicolon inside a string must not desync -------------
586	        stmts = _split_statements("INSERT INTO t VALUES ('a;b');\nINSERT INTO t VALUES (2);\n")
587	        check("splitter is quote-aware", len(stmts) == 2, f"got {len(stmts)}: {stmts}")
588	        stmts, _ = _prepare_body("-- only a comment\n")
589	        check("comment-only body yields no statements", stmts == [], f"got {stmts}")
590	
591	    print("\n--- migrate_db selftest ---")
592	    for name, ok, detail in results:
593	        print(f"  {'PASS' if ok else '**FAIL**'}: {name}" + (f"  [{detail}]" if not ok else ""))
594	    print(f"\nRESULTS: {len(results) - failures}/{len(results)} selftest cases pass")
595	    if failures:
596	        print("SELFTEST: FAIL")
597	        return 1
598	    print("SELFTEST: PASS")
599	    return 0

105	def _split_sql_values(tuple_body: str) -> list:
106	    """Split a `VALUES (a, b, c)` tuple body on top-level commas.
107	
108	    A plain `.split(',')` breaks on a comma inside a quoted string field
109	    (e.g. an authors field `'Smith, J.'`). This is a small state machine that
110	    tracks single-quoted-string state, including the doubled `''` escape, and
111	    ALSO tracks parenthesis depth, so a comma inside a nested function call
112	    in a field (e.g. `datetime('now')`, or a hypothetical `f(1, 2)`) is not
113	    mistaken for a field separator either.
114	
115	    Deliberately hand-rolled rather than `csv.reader(..., quotechar="'",
116	    doublequote=True)`: csv's quote-aware splitting alone would handle the
117	    `'Smith, J.'` case, but it has no concept of parenthesis nesting, so it
118	    cannot correctly split a field containing `datetime('now')` — that case
119	    is in this module's own false-negative test list (see selftest), so
120	    csv is not a drop-in replacement here. Kept as-is.
121	    """
122	    fields = []
123	    buf = []
124	    in_str = False
125	    depth = 0
126	    i = 0
127	    n = len(tuple_body)
128	    while i < n:
129	        c = tuple_body[i]
130	        if in_str:
131	            if c == "'":
132	                if i + 1 < n and tuple_body[i + 1] == "'":
133	                    buf.append("''")
134	                    i += 2
135	                    continue
136	                in_str = False
137	            buf.append(c)
138	        else:
139	            if c == "'":
140	                in_str = True
141	                buf.append(c)
142	            elif c == "(":
143	                depth += 1
144	                buf.append(c)
145	            elif c == ")":
146	                depth = max(0, depth - 1)
147	                buf.append(c)
148	            elif c == "," and depth == 0:
149	                fields.append("".join(buf))
150	                buf = []
151	            else:
152	                buf.append(c)
153	        i += 1
154	    fields.append("".join(buf))
155	    return fields

158	def _strip_sql_comments(sql: str) -> str:
159	    """Blank out `--` line comments and `/* ... */` block comments.
160	
161	    Comment markers found *inside* a single-quoted string are just text, not
162	    comments (honoured via `in_str`). Replacement is same-length-ish
163	    whitespace (newlines preserved) rather than deletion, so character
164	    offsets into the returned string still line up with the statement
165	    structure for the callers that scan it afterward.
166	
167	    This exists because `check_range_guards`'s old Form 1 scanned raw file
168	    text: a documentation comment like `-- an earlier batch wrote tier = 9`
169	    was indistinguishable from a real assignment and refused a legitimate
170	    migration (L1 false positive).
171	    """
172	    out = []
173	    in_str = False
174	    in_line_comment = False
175	    in_block_comment = False
176	    i = 0
177	    n = len(sql)
178	    while i < n:
179	        c = sql[i]
180	        if in_line_comment:
181	            if c == "\n":
182	                in_line_comment = False
183	                out.append(c)
184	            else:
185	                out.append(" ")
186	            i += 1
187	            continue
188	        if in_block_comment:
189	            if c == "*" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "/":
190	                in_block_comment = False
191	                out.append("  ")
192	                i += 2
193	                continue
194	            out.append("\n" if c == "\n" else " ")
195	            i += 1
196	            continue
197	        if in_str:
198	            out.append(c)
199	            if c == "'":
200	                if i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "'":
201	                    out.append(sql[i + 1])
202	                    i += 2
203	                    continue
204	                in_str = False
205	            i += 1
206	            continue
207	        if c == "'":
208	            in_str = True
209	            out.append(c)
210	            i += 1
211	            continue
212	        if c == "-" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "-":
213	            in_line_comment = True
214	            out.append("  ")
215	            i += 2
216	            continue
217	        if c == "/" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "*":
218	            in_block_comment = True
219	            out.append("  ")
220	            i += 2
221	            continue
222	        out.append(c)
223	        i += 1
224	    return "".join(out)

227	def _mask_non_numeric_strings(text: str) -> str:
228	    """Blank the *contents* of single-quoted string literals in `text`,
229	    except when the content is itself a bare integer (`'9'`) — SQLite's
230	    INTEGER-affinity coercion means a quoted digit is a real integer value
231	    at the storage layer (L2), so it must stay visible to the range regex;
232	    a narrative string like `'reviewer said tier = 9 is wrong'` must not, or
233	    its prose gets misread as an assignment (L1 false positive).
234	
235	    Used only to prepare an UPDATE statement's SET-clause text for the
236	    direct-assignment regex — never for the positional-INSERT path, which
237	    never text-searches string contents in the first place.
238	    """
239	    out = []
240	    i = 0
241	    n = len(text)
242	    while i < n:
243	        c = text[i]
244	        if c != "'":
245	            out.append(c)
246	            i += 1
247	            continue
248	        j = i + 1
249	        content = []
250	        while j < n:
251	            if text[j] == "'":
252	                if j + 1 < n and text[j + 1] == "'":
253	                    content.append("'")
254	                    j += 2
255	                    continue
256	                break
257	            content.append(text[j])
258	            j += 1
259	        raw = "".join(content)
260	        if re.fullmatch(r"-?\d+", raw):
261	            out.append("'" + raw + "'")
262	        else:
263	            out.append("'" + ("#" * len(raw)) + "'")
264	        i = j + 1 if j < n else j
265	    return "".join(out)

275	def _iter_update_set_clauses(clean_sql: str):
276	    """Yield the SET-clause text of each UPDATE statement in `clean_sql`
277	    (already comment-stripped) — the substring between `SET` and that
278	    statement's top-level `WHERE` / trailing `;` / end of string.
279	
280	    "Top-level" skips a `WHERE` or `;` that is inside a nested parenthesised
281	    expression (e.g. a scalar subquery) or a quoted string. This is the
282	    fix for the other half of the L1 false-positive class: a comparison in
283	    a WHERE clause (`... WHERE tier = 0`) is structurally never part of the
284	    yielded text, so it can never be mistaken for an assignment — no matter
285	    how the assignment-matching regex is written downstream.
286	    """
287	    for m in _UPDATE_SET_RE.finditer(clean_sql):
288	        i = start = m.end()
289	        n = len(clean_sql)
290	        depth = 0
291	        in_str = False
292	        while i < n:
293	            c = clean_sql[i]
294	            if in_str:
295	                if c == "'":
296	                    if i + 1 < n and clean_sql[i + 1] == "'":
297	                        i += 2
298	                        continue
299	                    in_str = False
300	                i += 1
301	                continue
302	            if c == "'":
303	                in_str = True
304	                i += 1
305	                continue
306	            if c == "(":
307	                depth += 1
308	                i += 1
309	                continue
310	            if c == ")":
311	                depth = max(0, depth - 1)
312	                i += 1
313	                continue
314	            if depth == 0 and c == ";":
315	                break
316	            if (depth == 0 and clean_sql[i:i + 5].upper() == "WHERE"
317	                    and (i == 0 or not (clean_sql[i - 1].isalnum() or clean_sql[i - 1] == "_"))
318	                    and (i + 5 >= n or not (clean_sql[i + 5].isalnum() or clean_sql[i + 5] == "_"))):
319	                break
320	            i += 1
321	        yield clean_sql[start:i]

361	def _extract_top_level_tuples(text: str) -> list:
362	    """Find each top-level parenthesised `(...)` tuple in `text` (the
363	    material after `VALUES`), returning each tuple's inner content with the
364	    outer parens stripped.
365	
366	    Quote state is checked BEFORE paren-depth bookkeeping on every
367	    character, so:
368	      - a `)` or `(` inside a quoted field (e.g. a source title
369	        `'ISO 21542 (2021)'`) never perturbs depth — this is what the old
370	        `re.finditer(r"\\(([^()]*)\\)", ...)` got wrong: it was paren-aware
371	        but not quote-aware, so it closed the tuple early at the first `)`
372	        inside the title, truncating it before the `tier` field.
373	      - a NESTED (non-string) paren, e.g. a function call
374	        `datetime('now')` inside a tuple, is correctly treated as part of
375	        the same top-level tuple rather than closing it early.
376	    """
377	    tuples = []
378	    buf = []
379	    depth = 0
380	    in_str = False
381	    i = 0
382	    n = len(text)
383	    while i < n:
384	        c = text[i]
385	        if in_str:
386	            if depth > 0:
387	                buf.append(c)
388	            if c == "'":
389	                if i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == "'":
390	                    if depth > 0:
391	                        buf.append("'")
392	                    i += 2
393	                    continue
394	                in_str = False
395	            i += 1
396	            continue
397	        if c == "'":
398	            in_str = True
399	            if depth > 0:
400	                buf.append(c)
401	            i += 1
402	            continue
403	        if c == "(":
404	            depth += 1
405	            if depth > 1:
406	                buf.append(c)
407	            i += 1
408	            continue
409	        if c == ")":
410	            depth -= 1
411	            if depth > 0:
412	                buf.append(c)
413	            elif depth == 0:
414	                tuples.append("".join(buf))
415	                buf = []
416	            i += 1
417	            continue
418	        if depth > 0:
419	            buf.append(c)
420	        i += 1
421	    return tuples

427	def _eval_int_expr(expr: str):
428	    """Evaluate a bare arithmetic literal expression (`6+3`, `9`, `10 - 1`)
429	    to an int, or return None if it isn't one. `expr` is validated against
430	    `_NUMERIC_EXPR_RE` first — digits, whitespace, and `+-*/` only — before
431	    it ever reaches `eval`, so this cannot execute arbitrary input (L2 case:
432	    `tier = 6+3` stores 9 in SQLite, same as a literal `9` would)."""
433	    expr = expr.strip()
434	    if not _NUMERIC_EXPR_RE.match(expr):
435	        return None
436	    try:
437	        val = eval(expr, {"__builtins__": {}}, {})  # noqa: S307 — input pre-validated above
438	    except Exception:
439	        return None
440	    if isinstance(val, float) and val.is_integer():
441	        val = int(val)
442	    return val if isinstance(val, int) else None

445	def _coerce_int_field(field: str):
446	    """Return the SQLite-affinity integer value of one INSERT VALUES field,
447	    or None if it isn't representable as a plain integer. Handles a bare
448	    integer literal (`9`) and a quoted integer literal (`'9'`) — SQLite's
449	    INTEGER column affinity coerces a well-formed integer TEXT literal to an
450	    integer at storage time (L2 case: `tier='9'`), so both are equivalent
451	    subjects for this range guard."""
452	    field = field.strip()
453	    if re.fullmatch(r"-?\d+", field):
454	        return int(field)
455	    m = re.fullmatch(r"'(-?\d+)'", field)
456	    if m:
457	        return int(m.group(1))
458	    return None

461	def check_range_guards(sql: str) -> list:
462	    """Return violations of the audit-enforced closed integer ranges.
463	
464	    Two forms, mirroring the deleted check_enum_guards:
465	
466	    Form 1 — direct assignment, `UPDATE ... SET col = N`. Scoped to the
467	    SET-clause text of each UPDATE statement (never a WHERE/ON/HAVING
468	    comparison — see `_iter_update_set_clauses`), over comment-stripped SQL
469	    (`_strip_sql_comments`) with non-numeric string contents masked out
470	    (`_mask_non_numeric_strings`). `N` may be a bare integer, a quoted
471	    integer (`'9'`), or a bare arithmetic literal (`6+3`) — all three are
472	    genuine SQLite storage values for an INTEGER-affinity column.
473	
474	    Form 2 — positional INSERT (`INSERT INTO t (a, col, b) VALUES (1, N,
475	    2)`, `INSERT OR REPLACE`, quoted/schema-qualified table names, multi-row
476	    VALUES, statements with or without a trailing `;`): unlike
477	    the deleted check_enum_guards' Form 2, this maps the guarded column's actual
478	    position in the declared column list to the same position in each
479	    VALUES tuple, rather than scanning the whole statement for suspicious
480	    literals — an integer column list nearly always contains *other*
481	    unrelated integers (years, attempt counts, ids), so a same-statement
482	    heuristic would false-positive constantly. Positional mapping avoids
483	    that. Tuple boundaries are found quote-aware-then-paren-aware
484	    (`_extract_top_level_tuples`), so a paren inside a quoted field (a
485	    source title like `'ISO 21542 (2021)'`) or a nested function call
486	    (`datetime('now')`) cannot desynchronise field positions.
487	
488	    KNOWN LIMITATION (not fixed — see module selftest / emit_data_migration
489	    audit report): an `INSERT INTO t VALUES (...)` with NO column list has
490	    no positional mapping this script can resolve without a schema/column-
491	    order reference it doesn't have, so such statements are not scanned by
492	    Form 2 at all. Not a regression — the pre-fix code had the same gap.
493	
494	    NULL is always permitted at either form — these ranges bound values that
495	    are *present*, not presence itself.
496	    """
497	    violations = []
498	    clean = _strip_sql_comments(sql)
499	
500	    for col, lo, hi, enforced_by in RANGE_GUARDS:
501	        if col not in clean:
502	            continue
503	
504	        # Form 1: direct assignment, scoped to SET clauses only.
505	        assign_re = re.compile(
506	            rf"\b{col}\b\s*=\s*(?:'(-?\d+)'|(-?\d+(?:\s*[+\-*/]\s*\d+)*))", re.I)
507	        for set_clause in _iter_update_set_clauses(clean):
508	            masked = _mask_non_numeric_strings(set_clause)
509	            for m in assign_re.finditer(masked):
510	                if m.group(1) is not None:
511	                    val = int(m.group(1))
512	                else:
513	                    val = _eval_int_expr(m.group(2))
514	                if val is None:
515	                    continue
516	                if val < lo or val > hi:
517	                    violations.append((col, val, lo, hi, enforced_by))
518	
519	        # Form 2: positional INSERT.
520	        for insert_m in _INSERT_RE.finditer(clean):
521	            collist_raw = insert_m.group(1)
522	            if collist_raw is None:
523	                continue  # no column list — see KNOWN LIMITATION above
524	            collist = [c.strip().strip('"').strip("`").strip("[").strip("]")
525	                       for c in collist_raw.split(",")]
526	            collist_lower = [c.lower() for c in collist]
527	            if col.lower() not in collist_lower:
528	                continue
529	            idx = collist_lower.index(col.lower())
530	            stmt_end = _find_statement_end(clean, insert_m.end())
531	            values_text = clean[insert_m.end():stmt_end]
532	            for tuple_body in _extract_top_level_tuples(values_text):
533	                fields = _split_sql_values(tuple_body)
534	                if idx >= len(fields):
535	                    continue
536	                field = fields[idx].strip()
537	                if field.upper() == "NULL" or field == "":
538	                    continue
539	                val = _coerce_int_field(field)
540	                if val is None:
541	                    continue
542	                if val < lo or val > hi:
543	                    violations.append((col, val, lo, hi, enforced_by))
544	
545	    # de-duplicate while preserving order
546	    seen, out = set(), []

580	```
581	SELECT x.extraction_id, x.claim_text, r.path, r.sha256
582	  FROM specification_syntheses ss JOIN synthesis_inputs i ON i.synthesis_id = ss.synthesis_id
583	  JOIN source_value_extractions x ON x.extraction_id = i.extraction_id JOIN scans s ON s.scan_id = x.scan_id
584	  JOIN retrievals r ON r.retrieval_id = s.retrieval_id
585	 WHERE ss.specification_id = :spec AND i.role = 'governing';
586	```

600	## 6. WALKABILITY ACROSS ALL TABLES
601	
602	One derived check over every table in `sqlite_master`: stage from the stage-map; FK edges from `PRAGMA foreign_key_list`; an id column is a column named like another table's single-column primary key; `up` = path to a base table; `down` = path to `specifications` not passing through base (base tables may). Re-run:
603	
604	```
605	python3 - <<'PY'
606	import sqlite3, yaml, collections as C
607	c = sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro', uri=True)
608	st = yaml.safe_load(open('governance/stage-map.yaml'))['tables']
609	T = [r[0] for r in c.execute("select name from sqlite_master where type='table' and name not like 'sqlite_%'")]
610	fk = [(t, f[3], f[2]) for t in T for f in c.execute(f'pragma foreign_key_list("{t}")')]
611	cols = {t: c.execute(f'pragma table_info("{t}")').fetchall() for t in T}
612	home = C.defaultdict(set)
613	for t in T:
614	    pk = [r[1] for r in cols[t] if r[5]]
615	    if len(pk) == 1: home[pk[0]].add(t)
616	adj = C.defaultdict(set)
617	for a, _, b in fk: adj[a].add(b); adj[b].add(a)
618	def bfs(s, goal, via_base):
619	    seen, q = {s: 0}, C.deque([s])
620	    while q:
621	        n = q.popleft()
622	        if n != s and goal(n): return seen[n]
623	        if n != s and not via_base and st.get(n) == 'base': continue
624	        for m in adj[n] - seen.keys(): seen[m] = seen[n] + 1; q.append(m)
625	bad = C.Counter(r[0] for r in c.execute('pragma foreign_key_check'))
626	for t in sorted(T, key=lambda t: (st.get(t, '?'), t)):
627	    fkc = {col for a, col, _ in fk if a == t}
628	    loose = [r[1] for r in cols[t] if r[1] in home and t not in home[r[1]] and r[1] not in fkc]
629	    up = 0 if st.get(t) == 'base' else bfs(t, lambda n: st.get(n) == 'base', True)
630	    dn = 0 if t == 'specifications' else bfs(t, lambda n: n == 'specifications', st.get(t) == 'base')
631	    fail = [d for d, v in (('up', up), ('down', dn)) if v is None] + ['orphan'] * (not adj[t]) \
632	         + [f'dangling:{bad[t]}'] * bool(bad[t]) + [f'unFK:{",".join(loose)}'] * bool(loose)
633	    print(t, st.get(t, 'UNMAPPED'), '-' if up is None else up, '-' if dn is None else dn, ' '.join(fail) or 'ok', sep='\t')
634	PY
635	```

656	## 7. ACQUISITION
657	
658	For any source and any parameter, with no container and no slug in the way:
659	
660	1. **Find.** The agent queries (an MCP search tool, an API, a catalogue, the Internet Archive). Before anything reads the response, `retrieval_log.fetch` (HTTP) or `record_file` (an MCP result or a local file) writes the bytes and a manifest line (`retrieval_log.py:203-230`). `log-search` records the query verbatim, the prior, its reason (slug, synthesis or mined source), lens codes, jurisdiction, language and counts, and cites the artefact; the `retrievals` row enters with it.
661	2. **Stage.** `add-candidate` for each result considered, citing the retrieval and a quote that must be in it (PIP-19).
662	3. **Admit.** Re-retrieve the locator with `fetch` (DOI → Crossref/PubMed → publisher → repository → Wayback `if_` form, `CLAUDE.md` §7); `add-source --retrieval`: fields and authors parsed from the payload; DOI de-duplication; verification computed; `resolve-candidate ADMITTED`.
663	4. **Read.** Fetch or record the full text; one `record-scan` row says "read for every parameter up to version N".
664	5. **Mine.** `observe-term` for each concept phrase, located in the bytes; `add-extraction` for each parameter the source bears on, in each lens it names: figures, arguments, findings, harms and stated absences.
665	6. **Organize.** `adjudicate-term` → `add-term` / `add-parameter` or decline; `grade-source`; `add-lens-match`; `relate-extraction`. A new parameter shows every earlier source as NOT-READ at once.
666	7. **Sort.** Queries over the views and the walk (band, tier, independent roots, recency). No stored order.
667	8. **Weigh.** `assess_cell.py --emit-sql`; Opus/Fable add divergence, conflict and connection syntheses.
668	9. **Emit.** `emit_batch_sql.py` → `emit_data_migration.py` → `migrate_db.py`.
669	
670	**What must persist for CLAUDE.md 5(c) and R10:** the bytes (committed under `retrieval-log/`), the manifest line written before the caller sees data, the `retrievals` row, and the NOT NULL pointers to it from `evidence_sources`, `observed_terms` and `scans` (and through scans, every extraction). A field typed from memory has nowhere to go: `add-source` takes no bibliographic flags when a parseable payload exists.
671	
672	**Code** (what cannot be a constraint or a writer refusal): `fetch`/`record_file`; a payload parser per structured API actually used [I did not count them]; byte decoding and `quote_in_artefacts`; the verbs; the engine; the renderer; `walk`; the write path; `run_checks.py` and twelve gates. **Data:** vocabularies, `tier_ladder`, bucket membership, the catalogues and the parameter list, mining screens (`governance/mining-screens.yaml`, LED-181), rulings, and the bytes. No per-source scraper, crawler or scheduled job.

-- 093_convergence_sources_junction.sql
--
-- SIXTY-NINE POINTERS THAT WERE STRINGS, GIVEN A REAL HOME.
--
-- `convergence_assessment` records which sources converge on a determination, and it has
-- been recording them as five JSON arrays of ref_ids inside five TEXT columns:
-- clinical_sources, co1_sources, co2_sources, down_weighted_sources, discounted_sources.
-- A ref_id inside a JSON string is not a pointer. It has no foreign key, so the database
-- cannot refuse a ref that does not exist and cannot refuse one that is later retired; it
-- cannot be joined, so every reader re-parses JSON in Python; and `schema_reference_audit`
-- cannot see it at all, because there is no reference in the schema for it to check.
--
-- Measured 2026-09-20 across this table and `specifications.governing_refs`: 107 ref_ids
-- were held inside JSON strings, all 107 resolving today, none of them protected. The
-- 2026-09-13 circulation clear is the precedent that makes this urgent rather than tidy --
-- it moved the ref_id mark REF-00982 -> REF-00970 with every gate green, because the
-- database was internally consistent and the contradiction lived between the database and
-- the record of what it had held. That is exactly the failure a string cannot resist:
-- delete a source and the JSON keeps naming it, silently, forever.
--
-- WHY A JUNCTION AND NOT A WIDER COLUMN. CLAUDE.md rule 5: "It is better to have a table
-- cell point to another table cell than to rewrite." The role (clinical / co1 / co2 /
-- down_weighted / discounted) is a property of the PAIRING -- this source, in this
-- assessment, weighed this way -- not of the source and not of the assessment, so it is the
-- junction's own column. The vocabulary is declared in its CHECK, which is where a
-- vocabulary belongs (rule 8), rather than implied by which of five columns a string
-- happened to sit in.
--
-- THE JSON COLUMNS ARE NOT DROPPED, AND CANNOT BE. Seven committed data migrations INSERT
-- them, and a committed data migration is immutable (rule 3), so dropping the columns would
-- break a rebuild from history. Rule 5 names the sequence for exactly this case --
-- "writer-retire, reader-retire, NULL forward" -- and this migration is its first step:
--
--   1. (here)  create the junction and backfill every existing row from the JSON.
--   2. writer  assess_cell.py writes convergence_sources and stops writing the arrays.
--   3. reader  validate_evidence_state.py reads the junction.
--   4. forward new rows carry NULL in the five columns; the five rows written before today
--              keep their arrays, because that is what the immutable migrations say they
--              held, and the junction now says the same thing in a form that can be checked.
--
-- This is deliberately NOT a parity check between the two homes. CLAUDE.md is explicit that
-- "a parity check is not a fix -- it makes a dual home survivable, therefore permanent." The
-- junction becomes the only home a writer writes and the only home a reader reads; the
-- arrays are frozen history, not a second live copy.
--
-- AFTER_DATA: 20260920060857
CREATE TABLE convergence_sources (
    convergence_id  INTEGER NOT NULL
                    REFERENCES convergence_assessment(convergence_id),
    ref_id          TEXT    NOT NULL
                    REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    -- The weighing is a property of the pairing, so it lives here. Vocabulary in the
    -- column's own CHECK, read by dbcore.check_values() rather than retyped by a caller.
    role            TEXT    NOT NULL
                    CHECK (role IN ('clinical', 'co1', 'co2',
                                    'down_weighted', 'discounted')),
    created_at          TEXT,
    created_by_session  TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (convergence_id, ref_id, role)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_convergence_sources_ref  ON convergence_sources(ref_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_convergence_sources_role ON convergence_sources(role);
-- Backfill, one INSERT per role, reading the arrays with json_each so the migration does
-- not re-list the ref_ids it is migrating. A ref_id in an array that no longer resolves to
-- evidence_sources would violate the new FK; none does today, and if one ever did the
-- migration failing loudly here is the correct outcome -- that is the whole point of the
-- constraint this table adds.
INSERT INTO convergence_sources (convergence_id, ref_id, role, created_at, created_by_session)
SELECT ca.convergence_id, je.value, 'clinical', ca.created_at, ca.created_by_session
  FROM convergence_assessment ca, json_each(ca.clinical_sources) je
